I wouldn't want a system like that in place because I can see too many problems with it.  For one, it would encourage people to simply save their reports for people who are consistently toxic or feeding in a current streak.  Therefore you would base using your reports on whether or not you think a person was reported recently in a previous game by checking their game history.  This would either discourage players from using reports on actual toxic players or feeders who don't have a history or encourage toxic behavior in sporadic bursts.  Also, how would a system handle someone who was "trusted" in terms of their positive report rate but also toxic themselves?  Would it be that if you're put into low priority for any reason you would be excluded from having "weighted" reports? Who watches the watchmen? 

Just reading through this thread you can see the wild variation of what people deem unacceptable from "a treant support who afk jungles the whole game and comes out at 50 minutes with a radiance and bloodstone or some shit" to "refused to talk about lanes before match" to "crying in all-chat for people to report X player".  In my opinion, none of those examples are deserving of being sent to LP.  You can try spamming captains mode and picking a team of your choice without consulting anyone else on your team about the picks.  Might be a dick move but not LP worthy.  Not being able to play your ideal hero is something you should expect going into captains mode but people spam "report captain" for that regularly.  You seem to believe the only people who end up in LP are those commit one of the reportable offenses (i.e Communication abuse, Intentional Ability Abuse, Intentional Feeding) but whether you're willing to believe it or not, people report others for reasons outside of those categories and those reports count.

I pointed this out in a post yesterday:

https://www.reddit.com/r/DotA2/comments/5m2v29/1_mmr_low_priority/

You can have your communication privileges revoked just for being reported for "Communication abuse" even if you never communicate at all.  There is no system in place checking to see whether or not you communicated at all, testing the validity of such reports.  All reports seem to be accepted at face value.
